runs.text: NLP group project. All quantitative claims come from the local frozen evaluation. Actual team names, contributions and narration require confirmation by the real members. Target narration length: approximately nine minutes.
English movie and business reviews receive positive or negative labels.
Does contextual pretraining improve over strong sparse baselines?
How well does a saved model transfer to another review corpus?
What training and inference costs accompany the measured gains?
Use case: support readers who need a first-pass positive/negative label for English reviews. Scope: binary English sentiment classification, not new architecture or production deployment.
24,000 selected examples with globally unique normalized hashes
Two movie corpora share a domain. Length, style and label construction also differ.
See data/audit.json and assets.lock.json. Training and validation labels serve model fitting/selection. Test examples retain official test provenance. Each sampled split is balanced.
Base pretrained weights plus a new sentiment head. No ready-made sentiment classifier.

TF-IDF uses training-only vocabulary and IDF. Logistic Regression estimates probabilities. LinearSVC produces margins. DistilBERT uses contextual self-attention and a two-class head. External pretraining prevents an architecture-only causal comparison.
Source-only validation selects hyperparameters and checkpoints.
Sparse models: 2 n-gram choices × 3 regularization values per source.
DistilBERT: 2 learning rates, 3 epochs and seeds 42 / 43 / 44.
Frozen sample manifests and 15 final model files precede testing.
TF-IDF fits source training text only. Direct transfer uses no target-label adaptation.

Sources: config.json, data/manifest.csv, per-model metadata.json, results/protocol.freeze.json. Thirty-six traditional candidate fits. Twelve DistilBERT training runs, including two learning-rate candidates per source and the two additional seeds for the selected LR. Fifteen final artifacts: six traditional plus nine Transformer. Optional learning curves excluded before testing.
DistilBERT bars average three seeds. Per-seed variation appears in the report, not as a test confidence interval.

Source: results/metrics.csv, source==target. Values are Macro-F1 on 1,000 fixed test reviews per dataset. DistilBERT averages three training seeds. Traditional models have one fixed fit. The report contains per-seed SD and the full predictions.
Rows = training source. Columns = test target. Values = Macro-F1. RT = Rotten Tomatoes.

Source: results/metrics.csv. Rows: training sources IMDb, Rotten Tomatoes (RT), Yelp. Columns: test targets in the same order. No target-data fine-tuning. Diagonal repeats within-dataset results. DistilBERT cells average three seeds. Corpus difficulty and text length confound pure domain-shift interpretations.
Paired comparison on the same test IDs
These intervals describe test-sample uncertainty for fixed models.

Source: results/bootstrap.json. One thousand paired, class-stratified bootstrap samples. DistilBERT seed42 and SVM selected in advance. Percentile intervals condition on the two trained models, exclude training uncertainty and do not correct for multiple comparisons.
One CPU, 4 threads, batch=1. 200 reviews × 5 repeats. Training and model-size costs appear in the report.

Source: results/benchmark.json. All models process the same 200 mixed-source review texts with batch size1, four CPU threads, 20 warm-up examples and five repeats. This slide uses IMDb-trained checkpoints, DistilBERT seed42. Timing includes cleaning and feature conversion, excludes loading/download. Training GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 Laptop GPU.
60 error / disagreement cases form the review queue.
Human reviewers must verify categories and explanations.
Long-review truncation is measured, not inferred as the cause of every error.

Source: results/evaluation.json for DistilBERT seed42 within-dataset confusion matrices, data/audit.json for truncation. False positives are negative labels predicted positive; false negatives are positive labels predicted negative. Error-review queue is a draft for genuine human checking.
pipeline.py: data isolation, source validation and checkpoint freezing
app.py: choose a training source and compare all three predictions
Results page: within-dataset scores, transfer matrices and CPU timing
Margin and probability outputs have different interpretations

Demo script: report/narration-script-zh.md. Show actual Python code, dataset audit, frozen artifacts, predictions and application. The demonstration fixes DistilBERT seed42. All narration must come from real team members, not generated voice.
DistilBERT has the highest mean Macro-F1
Results support this sampled experiment. Broader deployment requires new validation.

Source: report/slide-data.json, results/metrics.csv and report/experiment-report.md. Equal-weight means are calculated across three within-dataset Macro-F1 values. They are not pooled F1 or full-benchmark performance. Corpus/label differences, external pretraining and truncated inputs limit generalization. No unsupported novelty or causal architecture claim.
